The Ni55Ti45 (at%) (hereafter, base alloy) and Ni 55Ti42Hf3 (at%) (hereafter, 3Hf alloy) were fabricated using high-purity materials: Ni block (99.95 wt%), Ti sponge (99.76 wt%), and Hf particles (99.90 wt%) in an argon atmosphere. To achieve a homogeneous component, master alloy ingots underwent multiple cycles of melting (at least five times) in an arc-melting furnace.
After casting, the fabricated ingots underwent vacuum homogenization at 1050 °C for 24 h and were subsequently furnace cooled.
These samples were subjected to ST at 1050 °C, followed by rapid cooling.
Subsequently, the ST samples were subjected to prolonged heat treatments at temperatures of 400, 500, and 600 °C for 100 h.

The Ni55Ti45 (at%) (hereafter, base alloy) and Ni 55Ti42Hf3 (at%) (hereafter, 3Hf alloy) were fabricated using high-purity materials: Ni block (99.95 wt%), Ti sponge (99.76 wt%), and Hf particles (99.90 wt%) in an argon atmosphere. To achieve a homogeneous component, master alloy ingots underwent multiple cycles of melting (at least five times) in an arc-melting furnace.
After casting, the fabricated ingots underwent vacuum homogenization at 1050 °C for 24 h and were subsequently furnace cooled.
These samples were subjected to ST at 1050 °C, followed by rapid cooling.
Subsequently, the ST samples were subjected to prolonged heat treatments at temperatures of 400, 500, and 600 °C for 100 h.
